name: Grace Minseo Han
nationality: American; a U.S. citizen, born and raised in Washington State.
race_ethnicity: Asian, specifically Korean American. Her family background is one part of her identity, not a reliable guide to her opinions or interests.

residence.living_arrangement: Rents a one-bedroom apartment in Columbia City and lives alone. She likes having a quiet home base and enough room to read, cook, and host a friend for dinner.

education: She earned a bachelor's degree in psychology and later a master's degree in human-centered design and engineering at the University of Washington. She gravitated toward research because she likes listening for what people mean, not only what they say, and then making complicated information usable.

occupation.title: Senior user experience researcher
occupation.work: Works at a Seattle-based software company, studying how customers use its products and communicating findings to designers, engineers, and product managers. Her week includes interviews, analysis, planning research, and meetings. She is good at turning ambiguous complaints into questions a team can investigate.
occupation.work_history: After graduate school she worked in research and product roles with increasing responsibility. She is experienced enough to challenge a weak assumption in a meeting, but still likes doing interviews herself and does not especially want a job made up mostly of personnel management.
occupation.work_pattern: Usually works a hybrid schedule. Busy launches can create long days and make it harder to take leave at the ideal time; at quieter points she protects a few evenings from work.

gross_household_income.context: This is the gross income of her one-person household and comes primarily from her salary, with some variability from an annual bonus. Her income falls within the specified USD 100,000 to USD 199,999 range.

partnership_and_children_status.partnership: Single and not currently in a relationship. She dates occasionally but does not treat finding a partner as a deadline.
partnership_and_children_status.children: Has no children. She is not currently planning to become a parent; she considers that a personal decision rather than an assumed next step.

long_term_goals: Keep enough financial and professional independence to make choices without needing a particular employer or partner to support her.
Continue building expertise as a researcher while avoiding a career that is entirely meetings and management.
Stay within reach of her family and close friends, while keeping open the possibility of buying a home if the cost and location make sense for her life.

Take more trips that allow her to settle into a place for several days rather than rushing through a checklist. She and her mother have talked about visiting South Korea together, but have not set a date or itinerary.
style: She speaks clearly and fairly directly, usually giving enough context for a point to make sense. At work she asks specific follow-up questions and is comfortable saying that the evidence is incomplete. With friends she is warmer and more teasing, and often sends a concise text rather than making a long phone call. Her humor is dry rather than showy. When she is tired, she can sound brisk before she realizes how she is coming across.

personality.scale: These are fictional tendencies on an illustrative 1-to-5 scale, where 1 is low and 5 is high; they are not psychometric measurements.

openness.description: Curious about unfamiliar places, food, and ideas; prefers trying something new when she can still keep some control over the pace.

conscientiousness.description: Reliable about work and advance arrangements. She makes lists for trips and deadlines, but does not need every free hour planned.

extraversion.description: Enjoys close company and lively dinners, then needs quiet time afterward. She can be socially confident without wanting a packed calendar.

agreeableness.description: Considerate and usually cooperative, but not inclined to agree just to keep a conversation comfortable. She can be blunt when she thinks a decision is being dressed up as consensus.

neuroticism.description: Generally steady under ordinary pressure. Uncertainty about work or family can occupy her thoughts, but she tends to sort through it by making a plan or talking with someone she trusts.

preferences.reading: Enjoys reading for leisure and personal interest. She gravitates toward contemporary fiction, memoir, essays, and accessible nonfiction about design, cities, or technology. She often has one print or e-book in progress and uses audiobooks on walks or transit. She sometimes abandons a book that feels like homework, even if she has heard good things about it.
other_leisure_interests: Long neighborhood walks, particularly near water or through streets with small shops and older buildings.
Cooking at home from recipes, with enough improvisation that the result does not always match the photograph.
Occasional museum visits, independent films, and dinners with a small group of friends.
Easy day hikes and coastal outings; she likes being outdoors but is not motivated by extreme distances or summit records.

travel.what_she_wants: She wants a trip to feel like temporarily inhabiting a place, not collecting landmarks. She is happiest with walkable neighborhoods, public transit, local cafes and bookstores, interesting architecture, a museum or two, and meals that do not all require advance reservations. She likes having one clear plan for the day and room for an unplanned detour. She values a comfortable bed and a convenient location more than a luxury hotel.
travel.usual_pattern: Her job usually gives her around 18 paid vacation days a year. In a typical year she tries to fit in one longer trip of roughly a week or a little more, plus a domestic long weekend or two. She does not travel every time she has a free weekend: she also likes having days at home to recover, see family, and catch up on ordinary life. A longer international trip may happen less often when work is especially busy.
travel.companions: She travels well with one close friend who can make decisions without turning every choice into a negotiation. She is comfortable taking a short city trip alone and appreciates choosing her own pace, but for a longer trip she often prefers sharing meals and observations with someone she knows. Large groups with competing schedules wear her out.
travel.planning_and_spending: She researches neighborhoods, transit, and lodging before booking, and keeps an eye on the full cost of a trip, including meals and getting around. She saves specifically for travel and will pay more for a convenient base or a flight arrangement that avoids an exhausting itinerary, but she does not seek luxury for its own sake. She dislikes very tight connections and itineraries that depend on rushing. In cities she prefers walking and transit; for a rural or coastal outing she is willing to rent a car.
travel.likes_and_dislikes: She likes a mix of urban wandering and a smaller dose of nature. She is not drawn to cruises, resort packages, party-hostel atmospheres, or itineraries that change hotels every night. A quiet afternoon with no reservation feels like a real part of a vacation to her, not wasted time.
travel.past_trip: On a nine-day trip through Lisbon and Porto with a close friend, Grace arranged the lodging and transit while her friend found restaurants. They enjoyed the neighborhoods and food, but had planned more dinners than they wanted and ended up cancelling a few reservations. Grace came away preferring a looser schedule, with a couple of anchors and room to stop somewhere because it looked interesting. They split shared expenses and each paid her own travel costs.
travel.occasion_not_traveling: After a demanding stretch at work, she once chose not to use a block of leave for an out-of-state trip. She stayed home, saw family and friends locally, and found that she wanted quiet days more than another itinerary. She did not regard the time off as wasted.

beliefs.political_identification: Libertarian. She prioritizes individual liberty and is skeptical of government restrictions in both social and economic life.
beliefs.political_views: She is particularly alert to privacy and surveillance issues and favors adults having broad freedom over personal decisions. Economically, she is wary of rules that protect established interests or make it harder for new businesses to operate. She does not assume every private company acts fairly, and she can disagree with libertarians who treat any public intervention as automatically harmful. She is not a party activist and does not expect friends to share her politics.
beliefs.personal_values: Values personal autonomy, candor, competence, and having enough room in her life to change her mind. She prefers a reasoned disagreement to polite agreement that hides the actual issue.

skills: Conducting customer interviews and noticing when a participant's example does not fit the question being asked.
Synthesizing qualitative research without overstating what a small sample proves.
Facilitating meetings across teams with different priorities.
Writing clear research summaries and presenting findings to both technical and nontechnical audiences.
Planning travel logistics and navigating unfamiliar urban transit systems.
Cooking a handful of dependable weeknight meals and adapting recipes to what she has at home.
behaviors: Keeps a running list of books, restaurants, and places friends recommend, but does not feel obliged to work through it.
Usually reads or listens to something during her commute and makes time for a walk when the workday has been especially screen-heavy.
Checks in with family regularly and tends to handle practical arrangements when a shared plan needs organizing.
Budgets deliberately for larger discretionary expenses, including travel, while allowing herself occasional unplanned meals or books.
When a work discussion becomes vague, she asks for a concrete example; this is useful in her job and can sometimes feel overly pointed in casual conversation.

health.general: Generally healthy and able to maintain an active routine through walking and occasional easy hikes.
health.minor_concerns: Gets seasonal allergies and sometimes has neck or shoulder tightness after long stretches at a desk. She tries to stretch and take screen breaks but is not perfectly consistent.
health.wellbeing: A busy work period can leave her socially depleted. Time at home, reading, and a walk without an agenda help her reset.

relationships.family: Her parents live in the Puget Sound area. Her mother immigrated from South Korea as an adult, and her father grew up in a Korean American family in California. Grace understands familiar Korean phrases and can manage simple conversation, but is not fluent. She has an older brother who is married and has a young daughter; Grace enjoys being an involved aunt and appreciates that she can hand caregiving back to the parents.
relationships.friends: A small circle of long-standing friends matters more to her than having a broad social network. Maya, a friend from graduate school, was her companion on the Portugal trip and is someone with whom Grace can disagree without worrying that the friendship will end.
relationships.dating: She is open to meeting someone but is protective of her independent routines and does not want to force compatibility. She is not currently partnered.

other_facts.financial_situation: Her salary supports a comfortable but not extravagant life in Seattle. Rent and other housing costs are significant parts of her budget, so she weighs a potential home purchase against the value she places on flexibility. She keeps savings for emergencies and contributes to retirement accounts; she has no children or dependents in her household.
leisure_interests: Reading for leisure or personal interest.
Cooking, walking, and occasional cultural outings.
Travel that combines neighborhood exploration, good food, and unhurried time.
